+  ## AMD MI355X: InferenceX AgentX alignment
+
+  The MI355X single-node TP8 command follows the [SemiAnalysis InferenceX](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/) agentic-coding (AgentX) lane `kimik3-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-mtp` as of [PR #3833](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3833), whose final branch revision is [`6a0fe9d`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/tree/6a0fe9dea905dda24acfc8f8a190d9f65de987d3): the entry in [`configs/amd-master.yaml`](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/blob/6a0fe9dea905dda24acfc8f8a190d9f65de987d3/inferencex-e2e/configs/amd-master.yaml). The lane is a benchmark configuration: text-only, TP8 on one MI355X node, with the tool-call and reasoning parsers on.
+
+  **In the command builder.** Settings the lane uses at every concurrency are part of the MI355X TP8 command: `--load-format fastsafetensors`, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, `--max-model-len 1048576`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}'`, `--stream-interval 10`, `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm` and `VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=asm`. The lane's `--moe-backend auto` is vLLM's default selection, so the builder leaves that flag unset. Other AMD GPUs keep the general AMD profile.
+
+  - **Spec decoding** serves the lane's draft, the published [`Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark`](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark), with its attention on `ROCM_AITER_MLA` ([vllm-project/vllm#55966](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55966)), FP8 KV, probabilistic drafting and block verification. Draft length is tuned per concurrency in the matrix below.
+  - **C1 target quantization** applies `linear: fp8_per_channel` only to the dcp1/dcp8 concurrency-1 target cells, with the PR's ignored-layer list. The routed experts remain MXFP4; the DSpark draft remains BF16 with FP8 KV because it has its own unquantized model config.
+  - **Decode context parallelism** emits the lane's DCP8 pairing: `--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA`, `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`, `ROCM_AITER_FA` prefill and the direct DCP ops off.
+  - The **Simple** KV-offload option emits the connector the lane uses (`SimpleCPUOffloadConnector`, `kv_both`, `lazy_offload: false`).
+  - Select **Python** in the frontend selector to match the lane, which runs vLLM's default frontend.
+
+  **Per-concurrency tuning (guide only).** The lane retunes the following nine points. The builder keeps general values (`--max-num-seqs 128`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`, and effective `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` CUDA graphs); use the reproduction command below for exact benchmark cells. Every point requests `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` with breakable CUDA graphs disabled; because Kimi-K3 has no `torch.compile` submodule, vLLM resolves that mode to `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` at load.
+
+  | Concurrency | DCP | KV offload | Draft tokens | `--max-num-seqs` | `--max-num-batched-tokens` | `cudagraph_mode` | `VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH` |
+  | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: |
+  | 1 | 1 | none | 7 | 2 | 16384 | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 0 |
+  | 1 | 8 | none | 7 | 2 | 16384 | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 0 |
+  | 4 | 8 | Simple | 5 | 8 | 8192 | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 0 |
+  | 10 | 8 | Simple | 4 | 20 | 8192 | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 0 |
+  | 12 | 8 | Simple | 3 | 24 | 8192 | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 0 |
+  | 14 | 8 | Simple | 4 | 28 | 8192 | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 0 |
+  | 16 | 8 | Simple | 4 | 32 | 8192 | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 0 |
+  | 44 | 8 | Simple | 4 | 88 | 8192 | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 0 |
+  | 48 | 8 | Simple | 4 | 96 | 8192 | `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` | 0 |
+
+  DCP8 shards the decode KV read across all eight GPUs and uses the A2A backend. Simple offload points use 224.875 GB of host DRAM per rank. Every cell captures every even CUDA-graph size from 2 through `2 × concurrency × (1 + draft tokens)`. Agentic benchmark runs replace block rejection with the golden acceptance length for every draft point; synthetic acceptance is not suitable for serving or accuracy evaluation.
+
+  **Image.** The MI355X default variant uses `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100`, the rolling ROCm 10.0 nightly. This path needs [vllm-project/vllm#53940](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53940) (SiTUv2 a4w4 MoE routing) and #55966.
+
+  **MoE environment.** The lane exports the legacy names `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2_A8W4=1`, `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1` and `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0`. On its image the first is a deprecated alias for `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2`, vLLM removes `AITER_SITUV2_A8W4` at startup, and the a4w4 kernels do not read `AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND`, so the lane runs the same SiTUv2 a4w4 MoE path as the recipe's `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1`.
+
+  ### Reproducing one lane cell
+
+  This is the real-verification form, the one InferenceX's eval jobs use and the one to use for any serving:
+
+  ```bash
+  # One lane cell per server. For CONC=1, choose DCP=1 or DCP=8.
+  CONC=1
+  DCP=1
+  case "$CONC:$DCP" in
+    1:1|1:8) K=7; BATCHED=16384; OFFLOAD=0 ;;
+    4:8) K=5; BATCHED=8192; OFFLOAD=1 ;;
+    10:8|14:8|16:8|44:8|48:8) K=4; BATCHED=8192; OFFLOAD=1 ;;
+    12:8) K=3; BATCHED=8192; OFFLOAD=1 ;;
+    *) echo "CONC=$CONC DCP=$DCP is not a lane cell" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  esac
+
+  export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
+  export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1
+  export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_MOE_SITUV2=1
+  export VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm
+  export VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=asm
+  export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0
+  export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=0
+  export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER=0
+  # Benchmark-only and accuracy-sensitive (INT4-quantized all-reduce): not in the builder.
+  export AITER_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
+  # 1.56 TB of weights from shared storage, and long agentic prefills.
+  export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=7200
+  export VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200
+  # On MEC firmware older than 177 (rocm-smi --showfw), also export HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1.
+
+  GRAPH_MODE=FULL_AND_PIECEWISE
+  export VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0
+  MAX_SEQS=$((2 * CONC))
+  MAX_CAPTURE=$((MAX_SEQS * (1 + K)))
+  COMPILATION="{\"mode\":3,\"cudagraph_mode\":\"$GRAPH_MODE\",\"max_cudagraph_capture_size\":$MAX_CAPTURE,\"custom_ops\":[\"+fused_rms_norm_gated\"],\"cudagraph_capture_sizes\":[$(seq -s, 2 "$MAX_CAPTURE")]}"
+
+  EXTRA=()
+  if [ "$CONC" -eq 1 ]; then
+    EXTRA+=(--quantization-config '{"linear":"fp8_per_channel","ignore":["*kv_b_proj","*vision_tower*","*mm_projector*","*in_proj_qkvgfab","*f_b_proj","*fused_qkv_a_proj","*self_attn.g_proj","*.layers.0.mlp.down_proj"]}')
+  fi
+  if [ "$K" -gt 0 ]; then
+    EXTRA+=(--speculative-config "{\"model\":\"Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":$K,\"method\":\"dspark\",\"attention_backend\":\"ROCM_AITER_MLA\",\"kv_cache_dtype\":\"fp8\",\"draft_sample_method\":\"probabilistic\",\"rejection_sample_method\":\"block\"}")
+  fi
+  if [ "$OFFLOAD" -eq 1 ]; then
+    # The lane's node gives the connector 1799 GB of host DRAM (224875000000 bytes
+    # per rank); size cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank to your host. The fixed hash seed
+    # makes identical prefixes map to the same block keys on every rank.
+    export PYTHONHASHSEED=42
+    EXTRA+=(--kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"cpu_bytes_to_use_per_rank":224875000000,"lazy_offload":false}}')
+  fi
+  if [ "$DCP" -gt 1 ]; then
+    EXTRA+=(--attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA --decode-context-parallel-size "$DCP" --dcp-comm-backend a2a)
+  fi
+
+  vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --moe-backend auto \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+    --load-format fastsafetensors \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
+    --language-model-only \
+    --max-num-seqs "$MAX_SEQS" \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \
+    --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
+    --max-model-len 1048576 \
+    --enable-prefix-caching \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+    --stream-interval 10 \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens "$BATCHED" \
+    --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA"}' \
+    --compilation-config "$COMPILATION" \
+    "${EXTRA[@]}"
+  ```
+
+  The builder's **Simple** option keeps the repository-wide 220 GiB per rank and does not set `PYTHONHASHSEED`.

+  | ---: | ---: | --- |
+  | 7 | 3.84 | 1 (dcp1 and dcp8) |
+  | 5 | 3.62 | 4 |
+  | 4 | 3.36 | 10, 14, 16, 44, 48 |

+  ## AMD MI355X: disaggregated prefill and decode
+
+  This example uses one TP8/DCP8 prefill worker and one TP8/DCP8 decode worker on separate 8-GPU MI355X nodes. MoRIIO transfers the KV cache in READ mode; `MultiConnector` combines it with `SimpleCPUOffloadConnector` on prefill only. Both roles use the same target and DSpark draft checkpoints and FP8 KV.
+
+  These standalone commands are based on the 1P1D c48 configuration in [InferenceX#3582](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3582), with real block verification for serving and accuracy evaluation. They are separate from the command builder's NIXL PD configuration.
+
+  ### Prerequisites
+
+  - Make [moonshotai/Kimi-K3](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) and [Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark](https://huggingface.co/Inferact/Kimi-K3-DSpark) available inside every worker container. The commands below use `/models/Kimi-K3` and `/models/Inferact-Kimi-K3-DSpark` as example container paths; adjust them to match your deployment. Use identical checkpoint revisions on all workers.
+  - Use the worker and router images below, with the same worker image build on every node. The worker image contains the required vLLM support; no source patches are needed.
+  - Expose all eight GPUs, `/dev/infiniband`, host networking, and sufficient shared memory to each worker container. Allow locked memory for RDMA. The container's verbs provider must be compatible with the host NIC and driver.
+  - The prefill offload budget is 1,799 GB of host DRAM **across all eight ranks**, in addition to weight-loading and runtime memory. Reduce `CPU_OFFLOAD_BYTES` if the host cannot accommodate that allocation; the documented configurations use `1799000000000`.
+  - Set `SOCKET_IFNAME` and `RDMA_DEVICES` to your network interface and HCA list. `ROUTER_IP` and each `WORKER_IP` must be reachable addresses, not `0.0.0.0`. Allow router TCP ports 8000 and 36367, worker HTTP port 6100, and MoRIIO handshake/notification ports 26000–26007 and 27000–27007, plus the site's RDMA traffic.
+
+  ```bash
+  WORKER_IMAGE=vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly
+  ROUTER_IMAGE=vllm/vllm-router:nightly
+  ```
+
+  ### Start the router
+
+  Start one router before the workers. Discovery registers workers automatically; do not add static `--prefill` or `--decode` endpoints.
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run --rm --network host --entrypoint vllm-router "$ROUTER_IMAGE" \
+    --vllm-pd-disaggregation \
+    --kv-connector moriio \
+    --vllm-discovery-address 0.0.0.0:36367 \
+    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
+    --worker-startup-timeout-secs 7200 \
+    --policy consistent_hash \
+    --prefill-policy consistent_hash \
+    --decode-policy consistent_hash \
+    --log-level info
+  ```
+
+  ### Start the workers
+
+  Save the following as `kimi-k3-pd.sh` on each worker. Run it with Bash **inside the worker image**, with the devices and model paths described above.
+
+  ```bash
+  #!/usr/bin/env bash
+  set -euo pipefail
+
+  ROLE=${1:?Usage: bash kimi-k3-pd.sh prefill|decode}
+  : "${ROUTER_IP:?Set the router reachable IP}"
+  : "${WORKER_IP:?Set this worker reachable IP}"
+  : "${SOCKET_IFNAME:?Set the host network interface}"
+  : "${RDMA_DEVICES:?Set the comma-separated HCA list}"
+  CPU_OFFLOAD_BYTES=${CPU_OFFLOAD_BYTES:-1799000000000}
+
+  export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME="$SOCKET_IFNAME" GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME="$SOCKET_IFNAME"
+  export NCCL_IB_HCA="$RDMA_DEVICES"
+  export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0
+  export AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1
+  export VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_ASM_PADDING=asm VLLM_ROCM_AITER_MLA_DCP_VERIFY=asm
+  export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
+  export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_MAX_SIZE_BYTES_MB=256
+  export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1
+  export VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS VLLM_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=HND
+  export NCCL_DMABUF_ENABLE=0 HSA_ENABLE_IPC_MODE_LEGACY=1 HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=1
+  export PYTHONHASHSEED=42 PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1
+  export VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_A2A=0 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_Q_GATHER=0 VLLM_USE_DIRECT_DCP_KV_GATHER=0
+  export VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=7200 VLLM_EXECUTE_MODEL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200
+  export MORI_IO_SQ_BACKOFF_TIMEOUT_US=50000
+  export MORI_IO_QP_MAX_SEND_WR=16384 MORI_IO_QP_MAX_CQE=32768 MORI_IO_QP_MAX_SGE=2
+  export MORI_IO_TC_DISABLE=0
+
+  CUSTOM_OPS='["+fused_rms_norm_gated","+quant_fp8","+grouped_topk","+sparse_attn_indexer","none"]'
+  case "$ROLE" in
+    prefill)
+      MAX_SEQS=96
+      BATCHED=8192
+      KV_ROLE=kv_producer
+      COMPILATION="{\"mode\":3,\"cudagraph_mode\":\"NONE\",\"max_cudagraph_capture_size\":0,\"custom_ops\":$CUSTOM_OPS}"
+      ;;
+    decode)
+      MAX_SEQS=96
+      BATCHED=512
+      KV_ROLE=kv_consumer
+      CAPTURES="$(seq -s, 1 128),$(seq -s, 130 10 240)"
+      COMPILATION="{\"mode\":3,\"cudagraph_mode\":\"FULL_DECODE_ONLY\",\"max_cudagraph_capture_size\":240,\"cudagraph_capture_sizes\":[$CAPTURES],\"custom_ops\":$CUSTOM_OPS}"
+      ;;
+    *) echo "Role must be prefill or decode" >&2; exit 1 ;;
+  esac
+
+  MORI="{\"kv_connector\":\"MoRIIOConnector\",\"kv_role\":\"$KV_ROLE\",\"kv_load_failure_policy\":\"fail\",\"kv_connector_extra_config\":{\"backend\":\"rdma\",\"read_mode\":true,\"proxy_ip\":\"$ROUTER_IP\",\"proxy_ping_port\":\"36367\",\"host_ip\":\"$WORKER_IP\",\"http_port\":\"6100\",\"handshake_port\":\"26000\",\"notify_port\":\"27000\"}}"
+  KV_CONFIG=$MORI
+  if [ "$ROLE" = prefill ]; then
+    CPU="{\"kv_connector\":\"SimpleCPUOffloadConnector\",\"kv_role\":\"kv_both\",\"kv_connector_extra_config\":{\"cpu_bytes_to_use\":$CPU_OFFLOAD_BYTES,\"lazy_offload\":false}}"
+    KV_CONFIG="{\"kv_connector\":\"MultiConnector\",\"kv_role\":\"kv_both\",\"kv_load_failure_policy\":\"fail\",\"kv_connector_extra_config\":{\"connectors\":[$MORI,$CPU]}}"
+  fi
+
+  exec vllm serve /models/Kimi-K3 \
+    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 6100 \
+    --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+    --decode-context-parallel-size 8 \
+    --cp-kv-cache-interleave-size 1 \
+    --dcp-comm-backend a2a \
+    --moe-backend auto \
+    --load-format fastsafetensors \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
+    --language-model-only \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \
+    --max-model-len 1048576 \
+    --stream-interval 10 \
+    --enable-prefix-caching --prefix-match-unit 128 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 \
+    --block-size 128 \
+    --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_MLA \
+    --attention-config '{"mla_prefill_backend":"ROCM_AITER_FA","use_prefill_query_quantization":true}' \
+    --speculative-config '{"model":"/models/Inferact-Kimi-K3-DSpark","method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":4,"attention_backend":"ROCM_AITER_MLA","kv_cache_dtype":"fp8","draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"block"}' \
+    --max-num-seqs "$MAX_SEQS" \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens "$BATCHED" \
+    --compilation-config "$COMPILATION" \
+    --kv-transfer-config "$KV_CONFIG"
+  ```
+
+  On the prefill worker, replace the example addresses, interface, and HCAs with your site's values:
+
+  ```bash
+  export ROUTER_IP=192.0.2.10 WORKER_IP=192.0.2.11
+  export SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 RDMA_DEVICES=rdma0,rdma1,rdma2,rdma3,rdma4,rdma5,rdma6,rdma7
+  bash kimi-k3-pd.sh prefill
+  ```
+
+  On the decode worker:
+
+  ```bash
+  export ROUTER_IP=192.0.2.10 WORKER_IP=192.0.2.12
+  export SOCKET_IFNAME=eth0 RDMA_DEVICES=rdma0,rdma1,rdma2,rdma3,rdma4,rdma5,rdma6,rdma7
+  bash kimi-k3-pd.sh decode
+  ```
+
+  Prefill uses an 8,192-token batch budget without CUDA graphs; decode uses a 512-token budget with `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs. Both roles use a 96-sequence limit and four DSpark draft tokens. INT4 QuickReduce is a quantized collective optimization; validate accuracy for your workload and keep the same setting on all workers. The RDMA queue backoff is 50,000 microseconds (50 ms).
+
+  If long prefills encounter kernel scratch-allocation errors with limited free VRAM, allow scratch reclamation on the prefill worker with `HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=0 bash kimi-k3-pd.sh prefill`, subject to the host's ROCm/firmware compatibility requirements. This controls temporary kernel scratch memory, not KV-cache eviction or post-exit cleanup.
+
+  ### Scaling and concurrency tuning
+
+  For 1P2D or 1P3D, run the decode command on additional nodes with their own `WORKER_IP`. Discovery registers each worker automatically; the port ranges can be reused on separate hosts. These are router-balanced replicas, not a cross-node TP group.
+
+  Let `C` be the expected global client concurrency, `N` the number of decode workers, and `K` the draft length (4 here). Use the following as capacity-planning starting points, not fixed batch sizes or guaranteed optimal settings:
+
+  ```text
+  P max-num-seqs = 2 * C
+  D max-num-seqs = ceil(2 * C / N)
+  D graph max G = (K + 1) * C
+  ```
+
+  Set `MAX_SEQS` in each role's branch accordingly. The factor of two provides scheduling headroom. For decode, set `max_cudagraph_capture_size` to `G`, keeping it within the decode token budget. In `CAPTURES`, include every size from 1 through the smaller of `G` and the next power of two at or above `2 * C`, then larger multiples of 10 up to `G`; include `G` itself if needed.
+
+  At low concurrency, `G = (K + 1) * D max-num-seqs` with dense captures from 1 through `G` is an alternative.
+
+  The configurations below range from throughput-oriented to latency-oriented. All use TP8 workers, K4, prefill-only CPU offload, and the same P/D token budgets and graph modes as the example above. Capture every integer size from 1 through **dense**, then larger multiples of 10 through **max**.
+
+  | Topology | Global concurrency C | P/D DCP | P max-num-seqs | Per-D max-num-seqs | D graph dense / max |
+  | --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
+  | 1P1D | 56 | 8/8 | 112 | 112 | 128 / 280 |
+  | 1P1D | 48 | 8/8 | 96 | 96 | 128 / 240 |
+  | 1P2D | 48 | 8/8 | 96 | 48 | 128 / 240 |
+  | 1P2D | 24 | 8/8 | 48 | 24 | 64 / 120 |
+  | 1P3D | 24 | 8/8 | 48 | 16 | 64 / 120 |
+  | 1P3D | 12 | 1/1 | 24 | 8 | 40 / 40 |
+
+  The 1P3D C=12 configuration uses the low-concurrency graph formula (`G = 5 * 8 = 40`) and disables DCP with `--decode-context-parallel-size 1` on both roles. Keep P/D DCP and cache layouts matched. Benchmark concurrency sweeps and harness settings remain in the linked InferenceX configuration.
+
+  ### Verify routed inference
+
+  Wait for every worker to load and register with the router. Check each worker's `/health` endpoint and the router's `/v1/models`, then send a request through the router:
+
+  ```bash
+  curl --fail-with-body "http://${ROUTER_IP}:8000/v1/chat/completions" \
+    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
+    -d '{"model":"moonshotai/Kimi-K3","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"What is 17 + 25?"}],"reasoning_effort":"low","temperature":0.6,"max_tokens":4096}'
+  ```
+
+  Confirm that a final answer is returned, and inspect the prefill/decode logs for successful KV transfers and transfer errors. Health checks alone do not exercise RDMA. Preserve `reasoning_content` and tool calls when building multi-turn conversations, as described in the [model card](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3#6-model-usage).

+meta:
+  title: "Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct"
+  slug: "kimi-linear-48b-a3b-instruct"
+  provider: "Moonshot AI"
+  description: "Kimi-Linear is a 48B-parameter instruction-tuned MoE model (~3B activated) with a linear-attention variant supporting very long context (1M tokens)."
+  date_added: 2025-10-31
+  date_updated: 2026-04-17
+  tasks:
+    - text
+  performance_headline: "Linear-attention MoE with 1M-token context on a single node"
+  related_recipes: []
+  hardware:
+    h200: verified
+    mi300x: verified
+    mi325x: verified
+    mi355x: verified
+
+model:
+  model_id: "moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct"
+  min_vllm_version: "0.11.2"
+  architecture: moe
+  parameter_count: "48B"
+  active_parameters: "3B"
+  context_length: 1048576
+  base_args:
+    - "--trust-remote-code"
+  base_env: {}
+
+dependencies:
+  - note: "Pin vllm==0.11.2 — 0.12.0 has a known Kimi-Linear regression"
+    command: "uv pip install vllm==0.11.2 --torch-backend auto"
+
+features: {}
+
+opt_in_features: []
+
+variants:
+  default:
+    precision: bf16
+    vram_minimum_gb: 115
+    description: "Full precision BF16 on 4 or 8 GPUs (single node)"
+
+compatible_strategies:
+  - single_node_tp
+  - multi_node_tp
+  - multi_node_tp_pp
+  - multi_node_tep
+  - multi_node_dep
+
+hardware_overrides:
+  amd:
+    extra_args:
+      - "--no-enable-prefix-caching"
+    extra_env:
+      SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU: "1"
+
+strategy_overrides: {}
+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  Kimi-Linear is Moonshot AI's 48B-parameter instruction-tuned MoE model (`A3B` indicates
+  ~3B active parameters per token) featuring a linear-attention variant that enables very
+  long context windows (up to 1,048,576 tokens).
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - **Hardware**: 4 or 8 GPUs on a single node
+  - **vLLM**: `0.11.2` recommended. Avoid vLLM `0.12.0`, which has a known bug
+    `MLAModules.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'indexer_rotary_emb'`
+    that affects Kimi-Linear.
+
+  ```bash
+  uv venv
+  source .venv/bin/activate
+  # Install a stable version (avoid 0.12.0)
+  uv pip install vllm==0.11.2 --torch-backend auto
+  ```
+
+  ### AMD ROCm
+
+  The ROCm wheel requires Python 3.12, ROCm 7.0+, and glibc >= 2.35. Use the
+  ROCm Docker image when your host environment does not meet those requirements.
+
+  ```bash
+  uv venv --python 3.12
+  source .venv/bin/activate
+  uv pip install vllm==0.11.2 --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm/
+  ```
+
+  ## Running Kimi-Linear
+
+  The following snippets assume 4 or 8 GPUs on a single node.
+
+  ### 4-GPU Tensor Parallel
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct \
+    --port 8000 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
+    --max-model-len 1048576 \
+    --trust-remote-code
+  ```
+
+  ### 8-GPU Tensor Parallel
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct \
+    --port 8000 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+    --max-model-len 1048576 \
+    --trust-remote-code
+  ```
+
+  ### ROCm on 8x MI300X / MI325X / MI355X
+
+  ```bash
+  export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1
+  vllm serve moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+    --max-model-len auto \
+    --trust-remote-code
+  ```
+
+  If you see OOM, reduce `--max-model-len` (e.g. 65536) or increase
+  `--gpu-memory-utilization` (<= 0.95).
+
+  ## Client Usage
+
+  Once the server is up, test it with:
+
+  ```bash
+  curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -d '{"model":"moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Hello!"}]}'
+  ```
+
+  ## Troubleshooting
+
+  - **`MLAModules.__init__() missing 1 required positional argument: 'indexer_rotary_emb'`**:
+    Known bug in vLLM 0.12.0 affecting Kimi-Linear. Pin to `vllm==0.11.2` instead.
+  - **OOM**: Reduce `--max-model-len` or increase `--gpu-memory-utilization` up to 0.95.
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct on Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct)

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B is a hybrid-Mamba MoE model (30B total, ~3B active) with
+  FP8 and BF16 variants. It supports DGX Spark and Jetson Thor in addition to standard
+  Hopper/Blackwell servers.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - Hardware: 1x H100/H200 or comparable; DGX Spark, Jetson Thor, and Intel Arc Pro B60/B70 supported
+  - vLLM >= 0.17.0 (0.28.0 recommended for full support)
+  - Docker with NVIDIA Container Toolkit (recommended)
+
+  ### Pull Docker Image
+
+  ```bash
+  docker pull --platform linux/amd64 vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0
+  docker tag vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0 vllm/vllm-openai:deploy
+  ```
+
+  DGX Spark users can build from source (see README) or use the NGC image:
+
+  ```bash
+  docker pull nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:25.12.post1-py3
+  ```
+
+  Jetson Thor:
+
+  ```bash
+  docker pull ghcr.io/nvidia-ai-iot/vllm:latest-jetson-thor
+  ```
+
+  Intel XPU (B60 / B70):
+
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest
+  ```
+
+  ## Launch commands
+
+  FP8 with FlashInfer MoE backend (Blackwell/Hopper):
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --async-scheduling \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+    --moe-backend flashinfer_cutlass
+  ```
+
+  BF16 (with reasoning + tool parsers — typical for Spark/Thor):
+
+  ```bash
+  wget https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16/resolve/main/nano_v3_reasoning_parser.py
+
+  vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-BF16 \
+    --max-num-seqs 8 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+    --max-model-len 262144 \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
+    --reasoning-parser-plugin nano_v3_reasoning_parser.py \
+    --reasoning-parser nano_v3
+  ```
+
+  ### Intel XPU (B60, B70)
+
+  Validated on 4× Intel Arc Pro B60 / B70 (B60 24 GB, B70 32 GB per card) with the
+  official vLLM XPU image `vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest`.
+
+  FP8:
+  ```bash
+  docker run --device /dev/dri \
+    -v /dev/dri/by-path:/dev/dri/by-path --shm-size=16g \
+    --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
+    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+    vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest \
+    nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8 \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --async-scheduling \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
+    --enforce-eager \
+    --max-model-len 8192
+  ```
+
+  BF16:
+  ```bash
+  docker run --device /dev/dri \
+    -v /dev/dri/by-path:/dev/dri/by-path --shm-size=16g \
+    --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  NVIDIA Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B is a hybrid-Mamba latent-MoE model (~120B total,
+  ~12B active per token) trained for general reasoning, tool use, and agentic workflows.
+  It supports a 1M-token context window and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP). Variants ship
+  in BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 (Blackwell). A pre-RL Base BF16 checkpoint is also available
+  for downstream fine-tuning.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - Hardware: 4-8x H100/H200/B200/RTX Pro 6000, DGX Station, or DGX Spark
+  - vLLM >= 0.17.1
+  - Docker with NVIDIA Container Toolkit (recommended)
+
+  ## Launch commands
+
+  Reference command from the [vLLM blog](https://vllm.ai/blog/nemotron-3-super) (BF16, 4x H100, FP8 KV cache):
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --served-model-name nemotron \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
+    --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3
+  ```
+
+  FP8 weights:
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
+    --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3
+  ```
+
+  NVFP4 (Blackwell only):
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder \
+    --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3
+  ```
+
+  ### DGX Spark (GB10)
+
+  The NVFP4 variant runs on a single DGX Spark (GB10) at TP=1 inside the
+  `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0-ubuntu2404` container. The command below is the optimal
+  config tuned end-to-end on DGX Spark: the full 262144-token context fits with an FP8
+  KV cache and a float32 Mamba SSM cache (`VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1` allows the
+  long context, `VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION=high` keeps the Mamba scan numerically
+  stable), `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.8` leaves headroom in the 128 GB unified memory,
+  batching is sized for a single GB10 (`--max-num-seqs 8`,
+  `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`), `--load-format fastsafetensors` speeds up weight
+  loading, and MTP speculative decoding plus prefix caching are enabled for lower
+  latency:
+
+  ```bash
+  # Use container: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0-ubuntu2404
+
+  VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION="high" \
+  VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 \
+  vllm serve nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-NVFP4 \
+      --host 0.0.0.0 \
+      --port 8000 \
+      --max-model-len 262144 \
+      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
+      --max-num-seqs 8 \
+      --load-format fastsafetensors \
+      --attention-backend flashinfer \
+      --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
+      --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+      --mamba-cache-mode align \
+      --mamba-ssm-cache-dtype float32 \
+      --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' \
+      --enable-prefix-caching \
+      --reasoning-parser nemotron_v3 \
+      --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+      --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder
+  ```

+
+  The NVFP4 variant runs on a single RTX Pro 6000 at TP=1. Requires vLLM v0.24.0 or later. A few notes:
+
+  - **Set `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.92`** to avoid an OOM at startup. If you encounter an OOM, try adjusting the value.
+  - **Set `VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION="high"`** to use high precision for the matmul operations.
+  - **Set `VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1`** to allow the model to use the full context length.
+
+  ```bash
+  # Use container: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0-ubuntu2404
+
+  VLLM_FLOAT32_MATMUL_PRECISION="high" \
+  VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 \

+      --max-model-len 262144 \
+      --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 \
+      --max-num-seqs 8 \
+      --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
+      --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+      --mamba-cache-mode align \

+    --num-warmups 20 \
+    --ignore-eos \
+    --max-concurrency 1024 \
+    --num-prompts 2048

+  - [vLLM blog: vLLM on DGX Spark](https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-06-01-vllm-dgx-spark)

+dependencies:
+  - command: 'uv pip install "fastokens>=0.2.0"'

+

+  reasoning:
+    description: "Nemotron v3 reasoning parser — per-request reasoning toggle with a configurable token budget"
+    args:
+      - "--reasoning-parser"
+      - "nemotron_v3"
+  tool_calling:
+    description: "Qwen3 Coder tool-call parser with automatic tool choice"
+    args:
+      - "--enable-auto-tool-choice"
+      - "--tool-call-parser"
+      - "qwen3_coder"
+  mamba_fast_ssm_cache:
+    label: "Fast SSM Cache"
+    description: "FP16 Mamba SSM cache with stochastic rounding — faster decode than the FP32 default; the Philox rounds control the rounding stream"
+    args:
+      - "--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype"
+      - "float16"
+      - "--enable-mamba-cache-stochastic-rounding"
+      - "--mamba-cache-philox-rounds"

+  spec_decoding:
+    description: "Speculative decoding — built-in MTP heads, the DSpark hybrid speculator, or the DFlash diffusion drafter"

+    description: "Full-precision BF16 reference checkpoint — MTP only (no DSpark/DFlash draft is published for BF16)"

+    extra_env:

+

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is a hybrid Mamba-MoE model — 30B total parameters, 3B active,
+  up to 1M context, distilled from Nemotron 3 Ultra and trained for popular agent
+  harnesses. It ships as an NVFP4 (W4A16) ModelOpt checkpoint, the default deployment
+  target, and a BF16 reference checkpoint.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - **vLLM:** 0.27.1 or newer — `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.28.0`
+  - **Hardware:** 1x H100, 1x DGX Spark (GB10), or 1x DGX Station (GB300)
+  - **Speculative decoding:** **MTP** (built into the checkpoint), **DSpark** (hybrid
+    autoregressive + diffusion) and **DFlash** (diffusion) are all supported. DSpark
+    gives the best latency on H100 and DGX Spark; for maximum throughput, serve without
+    speculative decoding.
+
+  ## Client Usage
+
+  Once the vLLM server is running, consume it via the OpenAI-compatible API. Reasoning
+  is returned separately from the answer, on `message.reasoning`:
+
+  ```python
+  from openai import OpenAI
+
+  # Set this to match the --served-model-name used when starting the server
+  SERVED_MODEL_NAME = "nemotron-3.5-lightning"
+  BASE_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1"
+
+  client = OpenAI(base_url=BASE_URL, api_key="null")
+
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model=SERVED_MODEL_NAME,
+      messages=[
+          {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
+          {"role": "user", "content": "Briefly explain: what is vLLM and why is it useful for large model inference?"},
+      ],
+      temperature=1.0,
+      top_p=0.95,
+      max_tokens=2048,
+  )
+
+  choice = response.choices[0]
+  print("Reasoning:", choice.message.reasoning)
+  print("Content:", choice.message.content)
+  ```
+
+  Reasoning tokens count toward `max_tokens`. If `content` comes back empty or `None`,
+  the reasoning trace consumed the entire budget before the model produced an answer —
+  raise `max_tokens`.
+
+  ## Notes
+
+  - **Speculative decoding**: DSpark is preferred on DGX Spark. On DGX Station, prefer
+    MTP — choose it in the Speculative Decoding panel above.
+  - **DGX Spark (GB10)**: the selectable config is the one measured on 2026-08-31 with
+    aiperf 0.12.0 on vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev130+g44fe2a392` — DSpark drafting 7 tokens at
+    `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.7`, `--mamba-cache-mode align` and fastsafetensors
+    loading, served from `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly`. On SPEED-Bench at 8K input / 256
+    output, concurrency 1, it reached 7,252 prefill tok/s and 93.3 decode tok/s at a
+    3.98 s mean end-to-end latency.

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a hybrid Mamba-MoE vision-language model with image and
+  video input. The profiles below follow the NVIDIA cookbook's configurations on
+  `vllm/vllm-openai:v0.31.0`. The page opens on the one-H200 NVFP4 configuration.
+  Every generated command uses the full Hugging Face model ID as its served name.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - Pull the pinned vLLM image and make the selected checkpoint available from
+    Hugging Face. LiLiCorr on DGX Spark also needs its separate draft checkpoint.
+  - The NVFP4 checkpoint's safetensors index reports 75.01 GB; the recipe's 91 GB

+  ## Hardware configurations

+meta:

+  slug: "nemotron-nano-12b-v2-vl"
+  provider: "NVIDIA"
+  description: "NVIDIA Nemotron-Nano 12B vision-language model with video support and Efficient Video Sampling (EVS)"

+  date_updated: 2026-04-17

+  architecture: dense

+  active_parameters: "12B"
+  context_length: 131072
+  base_args:

+    description: "Efficient Video Sampling (EVS) prunes video tokens; 0.75 means 75% pruning"

+    args:
+      - "--language-model-only"

+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL is a vision-language model with image and video support. It
+  includes Efficient Video Sampling (EVS) to prune video tokens and reduce compute. The
+  model is available in BF16, FP8, and NVFP4 (QAD) precisions.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - Hardware: 1x GPU (A100/H100/B200, etc.)
+  - vLLM: 0.11.0 does NOT include this model; use latest nightly or install from source
+  - DGX Spark: use `nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:25.12.post1-py3`
+
+  ### Install vLLM
+
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:nightly-8bff831f0aa239006f34b721e63e1340e3472067
+  # or for DGX Spark:
+  docker pull nvcr.io/nvidia/vllm:25.12.post1-py3
+  ```
+
+  ## Launch command
+
+  ```bash
+  export VLLM_VIDEO_LOADER_BACKEND=opencv
+  export CHECKPOINT_PATH="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16"
+  export CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0
+
+  python3 -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server \
+    --model ${CHECKPOINT_PATH} \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"fps": 2, "num_frames": 128}}' \
+    --max-model-len 131072 \
+    --data-parallel-size 1 \
+    --port 5566 \
+    --allowed-local-media-path / \
+    --video-pruning-rate 0.75 \
+    --served-model-name "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16"
+  ```
+
+  Flags:
+  - `--max-model-len`: reduce for shorter contexts to save memory
+  - `--allowed-local-media-path <root>`: limit local-file access
+  - `--video-pruning-rate <0..1>`: EVS compression; higher prunes more video tokens
+
+  ## Client Usage
+
+  Describe a video:
+
+  ```python
+  from openai import OpenAI
+
+  client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:5566/v1", api_key="<ignored>")
+  completion = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16",
+      messages=[{
+          "role": "user",
+          "content": [
+              {"type": "text", "text": "Describe the video."},
+              {"type": "video_url", "video_url": {"url": "file:///path/to/video.mp4"}},
+          ],
+      }],
+  )
+  print(completion.choices[0].message.content)
+  ```
+
+  ## Offline / LLM API
+
+  ```python
+  from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams
+
+  llm = LLM(
+      "nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16",
+      trust_remote_code=True,
+      max_model_len=2**17,
+      allowed_local_media_path="/",
+      video_pruning_rate=0.75,
+      media_io_kwargs=dict(video=dict(fps=2, num_frames=128)),
+  )
+  ```
+
+  ## Troubleshooting
+
+  - Set `VLLM_VIDEO_LOADER_BACKEND=opencv` (required for video inputs).
+  - OOM: lower `--max-model-len` or increase `--video-pruning-rate`.
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-BF16)
+  - [Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-FP8](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-FP8)
+  - [Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-NVFP4-QAD](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-Nano-12B-v2-VL-NVFP4-QAD)

+  ### Platform-specific notes
+
+  - **RTX Pro:** append `--moe-backend triton` (FlashInfer + RTX Pro bug).

+  - **DGX Spark (aarch64):** unified LPDDR5X memory; lower
+    `--gpu-memory-utilization` to 0.70 and reduce `--max-model-len` (e.g. 32768)

+meta:
+  title: "GPT-OSS"
+  slug: "gpt-oss"
+  provider: "OpenAI"
+  description: "OpenAI's gpt-oss family (20B / 120B) with MXFP4 MoE, attention-sinks, built-in tools via Responses API"
+  date_added: 2025-08-05
+  date_updated: 2026-09-22
+  tasks:
+    - text
+  related_recipes: []
+  hardware:
+    h100: verified
+    h200: verified
+    b200: verified
+    mi300x: verified
+    mi325x: verified
+    mi355x: verified
+    ironwood: verified
+    arc_pro_b70: verified
+
+model:
+  model_id: "openai/gpt-oss-120b"
+  min_vllm_version: "0.10.1"
+  architecture: moe
+  parameter_count: "120B"
+  active_parameters: "5.1B"
+  context_length: 131072
+  base_args: []
+  base_env: {}
+
+features:
+  tool_calling:
+    description: "OpenAI harmony tool-call parser with automatic tool choice"
+    args:
+      - "--tool-call-parser"
+      - "openai"
+      - "--enable-auto-tool-choice"
+  spec_decoding:
+    description: "EAGLE3 speculative decoding for accelerated inference"
+    args:
+      - "--speculative-config"
+      - '{"model":"nvidia/gpt-oss-120b-Eagle3-v3","num_speculative_tokens":7,"method":"eagle3","draft_tensor_parallel_size":1}'
+
+opt_in_features:
+  - spec_decoding
+
+variants:
+  default:
+    precision: mxfp4
+    vram_minimum_gb: 96
+    description: "gpt-oss-120b with MXFP4 MoE; fits on 1xA100 80GB, scales to TP 2/4/8"
+
+  amd_fp8:
+    model_id: "amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8"
+    precision: mxfp4
+    vram_minimum_gb: 80
+    description: "Quark-quantized MXFP4 weights with FP8 activations for MI355X (gfx950)"
+
+compatible_strategies:
+  - single_node_tp
+  - multi_node_tp
+  - multi_node_tp_pp
+  - multi_node_tep
+  - multi_node_dep
+
+hardware_overrides:
+  blackwell:
+    # vLLM 0.24+ defaults to FLASHINFER_TRTLLM_MXFP4_BF16. Use
+    # --quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8 to restore optimal
+    # performance on Blackwell.
+    extra_args:
+      - "--quantization-config.moe.activation"
+      - "mxfp8"
+  amd:
+    # vLLM 0.17.0+ replaces the old VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_* env knobs with
+    # --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN. HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM is
+    # required on GPUs with firmware MEC < 177; harmless to keep set.
+    extra_args:
+      - "--attention-backend"
+      - "ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN"
+      - "-cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=True"
+      - "-cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=True"

+  xpu:
+    extra_args:
+      - "--block-size"
+      - "64"
+      - "--enforce-eager"
+      - "--disable-sliding-window"
+      - "--no-enable-prefix-caching"
+      - "--max-model-len"
+      - "9216"
+      - "--max-num-batched-tokens"
+      - "9216"
+      - "--gpu-memory-utilization"
+      - "0.9"
+    extra_env:
+      TORCH_LLM_ALLREDUCE: "1"
+      VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN: "1"
+      VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD: "spawn"
+
+strategy_overrides: {}
+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  `gpt-oss-20b` and `gpt-oss-120b` are open-weight reasoning models from OpenAI. vLLM
+  supports NVIDIA H100/H200/B200, AMD MI300X/MI325X/MI355X, and Radeon AI PRO R9700,
+  with ongoing work for Ampere/Ada/RTX 5090.
+
+  Optimizations:
+  - Flexible parallelism (TP 2/4/8)
+  - Attention kernels for attention-sinks and sliding-window shapes
+  - Asynchronous scheduling for CPU/GPU overlap
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - Hardware: NVIDIA H100/H200/B200 (or A100 80GB for single-GPU), AMD MI300+
+  - vLLM >= 0.10.1
+  - CUDA >= 12.8 if building from source (must match between install and serving)
+
+  ### Install vLLM
+
+  ```bash
+  uv venv
+  source .venv/bin/activate
+  uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto
+  ```
+
+  Docker quickstart:
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run --gpus all -p 8000:8000 --ipc=host vllm/vllm-openai --model openai/gpt-oss-20b
+  ```
+
+  AMD ROCm wheels:
+
+  ```bash
+  uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm
+  ```
+
+  Intel XPU (Arc Pro B70):
+
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest
+  ```
+
+  ## Launch commands
+
+  A100 (single card, default TRITON_ATTN + Marlin MXFP4 MoE):
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-120b
+  vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-120b --tensor-parallel-size 4
+  ```
+
+  Blackwell (B200) with FlashInfer MXFP4+MXFP8 MoE:
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-120b --config GPT-OSS_Blackwell.yaml --tensor-parallel-size 1
+  ```
+
+  On vLLM v0.28.0+ the FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP4 MoE path is selected automatically on Blackwell; it can be pinned explicitly with `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8`.
+
+  Hopper (H100/H200): same as Blackwell without `kv-cache-dtype` and without the FlashInfer MoE flags.
+
+  TPU v7 (Ironwood), verified on a `tpu7x-standard-4t` host (topology `2x2x1`, TP=2 × DP=4). Served via the OpenAI API-server entrypoint from the nightly TPU image (e.g. `vllm/vllm-tpu:nightly-20260316-e778980-57a314d`):
+
+  ```bash
+  export TPU_BACKEND_TYPE=jax
+  export MODEL_IMPL_TYPE=vllm
+  export HF_HOME=/data
+  export HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN=<your HF token>
+  vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-120b \
+    --host 0.0.0.0 \
+    --port 8000 \
+    --seed 42 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
+    --data-parallel-size 4 \
+    --max-model-len 9216 \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
+    --max-num-seqs 2048 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.86 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+    --load-format runai_streamer \
+    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
+    --async-scheduling
+  ```
+
+  AMD MI300X/MI325X:
+
+  ```bash
+  export HSA_NO_SCRATCH_RECLAIM=1
+  export AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS=0
+  export VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1
+  export VLLM_ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
+
+  vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-120b \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+    --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN \
+    -cc.pass_config.fuse_rope_kvcache=True \
+    -cc.use_inductor_graph_partition=True \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 \
+    --block-size 64
+  ```
+
+  Intel Arc Pro B70 (4x 32 GB, TP=4), MXFP4 weights via the official XPU image:
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run --device /dev/dri \
+    -v /dev/dri/by-path:/dev/dri/by-path --shm-size=16g \
+    --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
+    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+    -e TORCH_LLM_ALLREDUCE=1 \
+    -e VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 \
+    -e VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD=spawn \
+    vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest \
+    openai/gpt-oss-120b \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
+    --block-size 64 \
+    --enforce-eager \
+    --disable-sliding-window \
+    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
+    --max-model-len 9216 \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 9216 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9
+  ```
+
+  ## Tool Use
+
+  `/v1/responses` endpoint supports built-in tools (browsing, python, MCP). Setup
+  requires `uv pip install gpt-oss` and either docker (for Python sandbox) or
+  `PYTHON_EXECUTION_BACKEND=dangerously_use_uv`. For demo tools:
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve ... --tool-server demo
+  ```
+
+  For user-defined function calling:
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve ... --tool-call-parser openai --enable-auto-tool-choice
+  ```
+
+  ## Client Usage
+
+  ```python
+  from openai import OpenAI
+
+  client = OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1")
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="openai/gpt-oss-120b",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Explain sinks attention."}],
+  )
+  print(response.choices[0].message.content)
+  ```
+
+  ## Accuracy Evaluation
+
+  OpenAI recommends evaluating with the gpt-oss reference library:
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-120b \
+    --tensor_parallel_size 8 --max-model-len 131072 \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 10240 --max-num-seqs 128 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 --no-enable-prefix-caching
+
+  mkdir -p /tmp/gpqa_openai
+  OPENAI_API_KEY=empty python -m gpt_oss.evals \
+    --model openai/gpt-oss-120b --eval gpqa --n-threads 128
+  ```
+
+  Reproduced scores (120B): Low 65.3 / 51.2; Mid 72.4 / 79.6; High 79.4 / 93.0 (GPQA / AIME25).
+
+  ## Troubleshooting
+
+  - **Attention sinks dtype error on Blackwell:** pass `--quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8` and `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`.
+  - **`tl.language not defined`:** make sure no extra Triton (e.g., pytorch-triton) is installed.
+  - **H100 TP1 OOM:** `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.95 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024`.
+  - **Harmony vocab download failure:** pre-download tiktoken files and set `TIKTOKEN_ENCODINGS_BASE`.
+
+  ## Known Limitations
+
+  - Responses API: streaming is basic, annotations/citations unsupported, usage accounting returns zeros.
+  - Function calling currently supports only `tool_choice="auto"`.
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [gpt-oss-120b](https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-120b)
+  - [gpt-oss-20b](https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-20b)
+  - [amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8](https://huggingface.co/amd/gpt-oss-120b-w-mxfp4-a-fp8)
+  - [Eagle3 draft model](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/gpt-oss-120b-Eagle3-v3)
+  - [gpt-oss-120b on Ironwood (TPU v7)](https://github.com/AI-Hypercomputer/tpu-recipes/tree/main/inference/ironwood/vLLM/GPT-OSS)

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  [`gpt-oss-20b`](https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-20b) is OpenAI's smaller open-weight reasoning model: 21B total parameters with 3.6B activated per token across 32 experts (top-4 routing), shipped with native MXFP4 quantization on the MoE weights. It targets lower-latency and on-device use cases — the model loads in ~16GB of VRAM, runs on a single H100/H200/B200 or AMD MI300X/MI325X/MI355X, and supports the same harmony chat format, configurable reasoning effort (low / medium / high), and built-in tools (browser, python, function calling) as its larger sibling [`gpt-oss-120b`](https://huggingface.co/openai/gpt-oss-120b).
+
+  Architectural notes:
+  - 24 layers alternating sliding-window (window=128) and full attention.
+  - YaRN rope scaling (factor=32) extending 4K → 131K context.
+  - MXFP4 quant on `model.layers.*.mlp` experts; attention, router, embeddings stay in BF16.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - Hardware: NVIDIA H100/H200/B200, AMD MI300X/MI325X/MI355X, Intel XPU B60/B70, or 4x Xeon 6 CPUs.

+  source .venv/bin/activate
+  uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto
+  ```
+
+  ### pip (Intel Xeon 6 CPUs)

+  For Intel and AMD x86 CPUs, follow the
+  [CPU pre-built wheels](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/getting_started/installation/cpu/#pre-built-wheels)
+  installation instructions.
+
+  ### Docker (Intel Xeon 6 CPUs)
+
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-x86_64
+  ```
+
+  Docker quickstart:
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run --gpus all -p 8000:8000 --ipc=host vllm/vllm-openai --model openai/gpt-oss-20b
+  ```
+
+  AMD ROCm wheels:
+
+  ```bash
+  uv pip install vllm --extra-index-url https://wheels.vllm.ai/rocm
+  ```
+
+  Intel XPU (B60 / B70):
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-xpu:latest
+  ```
+
+  ## Launch commands
+
+  Single GPU (default — works on any 16GB+ card):
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b
+  ```
+
+  ### Intel Xeon 6
+
+  Choose the tensor parallel size based on the system topology and deployment
+  requirements. Add `--tensor-parallel-size <N>` when needed; the recipe does
+  not prescribe a Xeon 6 TP value or hard-code NUMA node IDs.
+
+  ```bash
+
+  vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8
+  ```
+
+  Docker:
+
+  ```bash
+  docker run \
+    --privileged --ipc=host -p 8000:8000 \
+    -v ~/.cache/huggingface:/root/.cache/huggingface \
+    vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-x86_64 openai/gpt-oss-20b \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
+    --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
+    --gpu-memory-utilization 0.8 \
+    --tool-call-parser openai \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice

+
+  Blackwell (B200) with FlashInfer MXFP4+MXFP8 MoE:

+  vllm serve openai/gpt-oss-20b
+  ```

+  On vLLM v0.28.0+ the FlashInfer TRTLLM MXFP4 MoE path is selected automatically on Blackwell; it can be pinned explicitly with `--moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm --quantization-config.moe.activation mxfp8`.

+

+
+  ## Reasoning effort
+
+  gpt-oss exposes three reasoning levels — low, medium, high — selected via the system prompt:
+
+  ```python
+  from openai import OpenAI
+
+  client = OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1")
+  response = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="openai/gpt-oss-20b",

+          {"role": "user", "content": "Explain why eigenvalues matter."},
+      ],
+  )
+  print(response.choices[0].message.content)

+  provider: "MiniCPM (OpenBMB)"
+  description: "MiniCPM-V 4.6 (1.3B) — pocket-sized multimodal LLM for ultra-efficient single-image, multi-image, and video understanding, built on SigLIP2-400M + a Qwen3.5-0.8B hybrid-attention backbone"
+  date_added: 2026-06-02

+dependencies:
+  - note: "MiniCPM-V 4.6 ships as a standalone architecture (MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration) only in transformers >= 5.7.0"
+    command: 'uv pip install -U "transformers>=5.7.0"'

+    command: 'uv pip install -U "vllm[video]"'
+    optional: true
+
+features:
+  tool_calling:
+    description: "Function/tool calling via the qwen3_coder parser (the v4.6 chat template emits Qwen3-Coder-style <tool_call> blocks)"
+    args:
+      - "--enable-auto-tool-choice"
+      - "--tool-call-parser"
+      - "qwen3_coder"
+
+opt_in_features: []
+
+variants:
+  default:
+    precision: bf16
+    vram_minimum_gb: 4
+    description: "BF16 weights (~1.3B params) — tiny footprint, runs comfortably on a single consumer GPU"
+
+compatible_strategies:
+  - single_node_tp
+  - multi_node_tp
+
+strategy_overrides:
+  single_node_tp:
+    tp: 1
+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  **MiniCPM-V 4.6** is OpenBMB's most edge-friendly multimodal model to date.
+  It pairs a **SigLIP2-400M** vision encoder with a **Qwen3.5-0.8B** hybrid
+  linear/full-attention language backbone (~1.3B params total). It handles
+  single-image, multi-image, and video understanding, and introduces **mixed
+  4×/16× visual token compression** — switch the `downsample_mode` per request
+  to trade accuracy for speed.
+
+  > MiniCPM-V 4.6 ships as **two independent checkpoints** — this recipe covers
+  > the Instruct model (`openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6`). For chain-of-thought output,
+  > use the separate `openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6-Thinking` checkpoint instead (unlike
+  > v4.5, the mode is no longer toggled at runtime).
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - **vLLM ≥ 0.22.0** — the `MiniCPMV4_6ForConditionalGeneration` architecture
+    landed via [PR #43213](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43213)
+    (merged 2026-05-22) and first shipped in the v0.22.0 release. No fork is
+    required.
+  - **transformers ≥ 5.7.0** — the model is merged as a standalone architecture
+    only in this version.
+  - For video inputs, install the `vllm[video]` extra.
+
+  ## Launch command
+
+  Use the command builder above. The baseline is simply:
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6 --trust-remote-code --port 8000
+  ```
+
+  Enable the **Tool calling** feature to add `--enable-auto-tool-choice
+  --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder`. The model emits a Qwen3-Coder-style
+  `<tool_call>` block inside the message content.
+
+  At 1.3B params the model fits on a single GPU (TP=1). v4.6 supports context up
+  to 256K, but start with a smaller `--max-model-len` (e.g. `8192`) and raise it
+  to fit your GPU memory and workload.
+
+  ## Client usage
+
+  **Image:**
+
+  ```bash
+  curl -s http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
+    "model": "openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6",
+    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": [
+      {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/openbmb/DemoCase/resolve/main/refract.png"}},
+      {"type": "text", "text": "What causes this phenomenon?"}

+  }'
+  ```
+
+  > **Stop tokens:** v4.6 uses the Qwen3.5 backbone with a new vocab. If you see
+  > runaway generations, pass `"stop_token_ids": [248044, 248046]` in your
+  > request body.
+
+  ## References

+  - [Model card](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6)

+meta:
+  title: "MiniCPM5-1B"
+  slug: "minicpm5-1b"
+  provider: "MiniCPM (OpenBMB)"
+  description: "MiniCPM5-1B — dense 1B on-device LLM with hybrid Think/No-Think reasoning, native 128K context, and strong agentic tool use, built on the standard Llama architecture"
+  date_added: 2026-06-02
+  date_updated: 2026-06-02
+  tasks:
+    - text
+  performance_headline: "1B-class open-source SOTA on tool use, code, and reasoning"
+  related_recipes:
+    - openbmb/MiniCPM-V-4.6
+
+model:
+  model_id: "openbmb/MiniCPM5-1B"
+  min_vllm_version: "0.21.0"
+  architecture: dense
+  parameter_count: "1.1B"
+  active_parameters: "1.1B"
+  context_length: 131072
+  base_args: []
+  base_env: {}
+
+features:
+  reasoning:
+    description: "Enable hybrid deep-thinking mode — the chat template wraps a <think> block before the answer. Recommended sampling shifts to temperature=0.9, top_p=0.95. Leave off for fast No-Think responses (temperature=0.7)."
+    args:
+      - "--default-chat-template-kwargs"
+      - '{"enable_thinking": true}'
+
+opt_in_features:
+  - reasoning
+
+variants:
+  default:
+    precision: bf16
+    vram_minimum_gb: 3
+    description: "BF16 weights (~1.1B params) — tiny footprint, runs on a single consumer GPU"
+
+compatible_strategies:
+  - single_node_tp
+  - multi_node_tp
+
+kv_offload_support:
+  offloading_cpu: verified
+  offloading_fs: verified
+
+strategy_overrides:
+  single_node_tp:
+    tp: 1
+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  **MiniCPM5-1B** is the first checkpoint in OpenBMB's MiniCPM5 series — a dense
+  1B model built for on-device and resource-constrained deployment, reaching
+  1B-class open-source SOTA on agentic tool use, code generation, and difficult
+  reasoning. It uses the **standard `LlamaForCausalLM` architecture**, so vLLM
+  loads it natively with no custom kernels or model-code fork.
+
+  Its headline feature is **hybrid reasoning**: a single checkpoint serves as
+  both a fast assistant (No-Think) and a deliberate reasoner (Think), toggled by
+  the chat template's `enable_thinking` flag.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - **vLLM ≥ 0.21.0** — MiniCPM5-1B is supported natively as of the v0.21.0
+    release. (For CUDA 12.x driver hosts, the cookbook suggests `vllm==0.10.1.1`
+    as a fallback.)
+
+  ## Launch command
+
+  Use the command builder above. The baseline is simply:
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve openbmb/MiniCPM5-1B --port 8000
+  ```
+
+  At ~1.1B params the model fits on a single GPU (TP=1). It supports the full
+  native 128K context; drop `--max-model-len` to `8192` / `32768` to free KV
+  cache on small GPUs, and set `--enforce-eager` if CUDA graphs OOM on a tiny
+  VRAM budget.
+
+  ## Reasoning modes
+
+  Toggle the **Reasoning** feature to serve with deep-thinking on by default
+  (`--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}'`). You can also
+  flip it per request via `chat_template_kwargs`:
+
+  ```bash
+  curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -d '{
+      "model": "openbmb/MiniCPM5-1B",
+      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Explain GQA in one sentence."}],
+      "temperature": 0.9, "top_p": 0.95, "max_tokens": 1024,
+      "chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": true}
+    }'
+  ```
+
+  | Mode | `enable_thinking` | `temperature` | `top_p` |
+  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+  | Think | `true` | 0.9 | 0.95 |
+  | No-Think | `false` | 0.7 | 0.95 |
+
+  ## Tool calling
+
+  MiniCPM5-1B emits **XML-style** tool calls. The vLLM-side `minicpm5` parser
+  ([PR #43175](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43175)) merged to `main`
+  on 2026-05-27 but is **not in v0.21.0 or v0.22.0** — those releases were cut
+  before the merge. Until a release bakes it in (v0.23+), load it as a plugin
+  from the [MiniCPM repo](https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM):
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve openbmb/MiniCPM5-1B --port 8000 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-parser-plugin /path/to/MiniCPM/tool_parsers/minicpm5xml_tool_parser.py \
+    --tool-call-parser minicpm5
+  ```
+
+  SGLang ships the `minicpm5` parser built-in and is the author-recommended
+  backend for tool calling.
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Model card](https://huggingface.co/openbmb/MiniCPM5-1B)
+  - [vLLM deployment cookbook](https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM/blob/main/docs/deployment/vllm.md)
+  - [MiniCPM Tech Report](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2506.07900)

+
+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  [PLaMo 3 NICT 31B Base](https://huggingface.co/pfnet/plamo-3-nict-31b-base)
+  is the largest PLaMo 3 NICT base model from Preferred Networks and NICT.
+  It is pretrained on Japanese and English data with a hybrid attention stack
+  combining sliding-window and full-attention layers.
+
+  This is a base checkpoint. Use completion-style prompts as-is, or fine-tune
+  it before deploying instruction-following or chat-style workflows.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - **Hardware:** H100/H200 80 GB for 4K context; use TP=2 for extra KV-cache headroom
+  - **vLLM:** >= 0.12.0
+  - **License:** gated Hugging Face access under the PLaMo community license
+
+  ### Install vLLM
+
+  ```bash
+  uv venv
+  source .venv/bin/activate
+  uv pip install -U vllm --torch-backend=auto
+  hf auth login
+  ```
+
+  ## Launching the Server
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve pfnet/plamo-3-nict-31b-base \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --max-model-len 4096
+  ```
+
+  With tensor parallelism for more KV-cache headroom:
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve pfnet/plamo-3-nict-31b-base \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --max-model-len 4096 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 2
+  ```
+
+  ## Client Usage
+

+  from openai import OpenAI
+
+  client = OpenAI(api_key="EMPTY", base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1")
+  resp = client.completions.create(
+      model="pfnet/plamo-3-nict-31b-base",
+      prompt="The future of artificial intelligence technology is ",
+      max_tokens=128,
+      temperature=0.7,
+  )
+  print(resp.choices[0].text)
+  ```
+
+  ## Troubleshooting
+
+  - **Out of memory on 80 GB GPUs:** add `--tensor-parallel-size 2` or lower
+    `--max-model-len`.
+  - **Gated repo errors:** accept the PLaMo community license on Hugging Face and
+    run `hf auth login`.
+  - **Repetitive or low-quality completions:** adjust sampling for free-form
+    generation, or fine-tune the model for chat or assistant workloads.
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Model card](https://huggingface.co/pfnet/plamo-3-nict-31b-base)
+  - [vLLM PLaMo3 support](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/models/supported_models.html)

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  [Laguna S-2.1](https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-S-2.1) is Poolside's
+  118B-total / 8B-activated Mixture-of-Experts model — the larger sibling of
+  [Laguna XS-2.1](https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-XS-2.1), built for
+  agentic coding and long-horizon work. It shares the `laguna` architecture:
+  mixed sliding-window + global attention (3:1 across 48 layers) with softplus
+  per-head gating and an FP8 KV cache, plus native interleaved reasoning and
+  tool calling.
+
+  ### Key features
+  - **Mixed SWA + global attention**: 36 sliding-window layers (window=512)
+    interleaved with 12 global-attention layers (3:1), each with per-layer
+    rotary scaling.
+  - **256 experts + 1 shared expert** with top-10 routing.
+  - **Grouped-query attention**: 8 KV heads, head dim 128, per-head softplus
+    output gating.
+  - **Native FP8 KV cache** to reduce memory per token.
+  - **Interleaved reasoning**: thinking blocks emitted between tool calls;
+    toggled per-request via `enable_thinking`.
+  - **Tool calling**: Poolside's XML-style tool-call protocol, parsed via
+    `poolside_v1`.
+
+  Same architecture as XS-2.1, so vLLM needs no S-specific code — support
+  lands with the shared `laguna` implementation.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  ### pip
+  ```bash
+  uv pip install -U 'vllm>=0.25.0'
+  ```
+
+  ### Docker
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:latest
+  ```
+
+  ## Variants and VRAM
+
+  Laguna S-2.1 is large: the BF16 weights are ~235GB, so unlike XS-2.1 the
+  default **does not fit a single GPU** — plan for a multi-GPU node or pick a
+  quantized checkpoint. Select one with the **Variant** control above:
+
+  | Variant | Checkpoint | Weights | ~Size | Fits on |
+  |---------|-----------|---------|-------|---------|
+  | BF16 | [Laguna-S-2.1](https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-S-2.1) | BF16 | 235 GB | ≥2× H200/B200, or a full HGX node |
+  | FP8 | [Laguna-S-2.1-FP8](https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-FP8) | Block-FP8 | 121 GB | TP2 on H200, or one B300; set `VLLM_BLOCKSCALE_FP8_GEMM_FLASHINFER=0` |
+  | NVFP4 | [Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4) | NVFP4 | 72 GB | single B200/B300 (Blackwell only) |
+  | INT4 | [Laguna-S-2.1-INT4](https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-INT4) | INT4 (W4A16) | 72 GB | single H200/B200 |

+  Quantization is detected automatically from each checkpoint's
+  `quantization_config`, so the launch command is identical — just swap the
+  model ID. All three quantized checkpoints ship an **FP8-quantized KV cache**.

+  [DFlash-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-DFlash-NVFP4),
+  [DFlash-INT4](https://huggingface.co/poolside/Laguna-S-2.1-DFlash-INT4) — to
+  pair speculative decoding with a quantized base at matching precision.
+
+  > **Context length.** The BF16 checkpoint supports up to 1,048,576 tokens;
+  > the quantized checkpoints are configured for 256K. The commands below use
+  > `--max-model-len 262144`; raise or lower it to trade context for KV memory.

+
+  ### Multi-GPU node (H200/B200, BF16)
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve poolside/Laguna-S-2.1 \
+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \

+  currently corrupts logits; other AITER operators remain enabled, while vLLM

+

+    --trust-remote-code \
+    --max-model-len 262144 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser poolside_v1 \
+    --reasoning-parser poolside_v1
+  ```
+
+  ## Controlling reasoning
+
+  Reasoning is **off by default** in the chat template. Enable it per-request:
+

+  client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8000/v1", api_key="EMPTY")
+
+  resp = client.chat.completions.create(
+      model="poolside/Laguna-S-2.1",
+      messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Write a Python retry wrapper with exponential backoff."}],
+      extra_body={"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": True}},
+      temperature=0.7,
+      top_p=1.0,
+      extra_query={"top_k": 20},
+  )
+  print(resp.choices[0].message.reasoning)
+  print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
+  ```
+
+  Or default-on with `--default-chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": true}'`.
+
+  The model's `generation_config.json` sets `top_k 20` (eval-certified
+  truncation) so clients that send no sampling params still get sane output.

+  `min_p`/`logit_bias` with speculation; use `top_k`/`top_p`.

+

+    --max-model-len 262144 \

+      --tool-call-parser poolside_v1 \

+  date_added: 2026-10-16
+  date_updated: 2026-10-16
+  tasks:
+    - text
+  performance_headline: "501B/23B-active MoE with hybrid sliding-window attention, 1M context, and DFlash2 speculative decoding"
+  related_recipes: []
+  # Beam's kernels (including a custom all-reduce) are CUDA-only and the
+  # only published build is the CUDA Docker image, so AMD is unsupported.
+  hardware:
+    b300: verified
+    h200: verified
+    mi300x: unsupported
+    mi325x: unsupported
+    mi350x: unsupported
+    mi355x: unsupported
+  # Open on the default variant's recommended hardware (NVFP4, TP4).
+  default_hardware: b300

+model:
+  model_id: "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B"
+  min_vllm_version: "0.33.0"
+  # Docker-only at launch: Beam support ships in this image before it reaches a
+  # vLLM wheel. A single-key CUDA map pins the one published build, so the
+  # CUDA toggle can't synthesize a nonexistent `-cu129` tag. Restore the pip
+  # path once a release carries the support.
+  docker_image:
+    cu130: "vllm/vllm-openai:reflection-beam"
+  install:
+    docker:
+      note: "Beam support hasn't landed in a vLLM release yet, so it ships only in this image. Use Docker until it does."
+    pip: false
+  architecture: moe
+  # 52 layers, 256 routed experts (top-8, moe_intermediate_size 2560), dense
+  # MLP in layers 0-2; release name: 501B total / 23B active.
+  parameter_count: "501B"
+  active_parameters: "23B"
+  # config.max_position_embeddings
+  context_length: 1048576
+  base_args:
+    # FP8 KV cache for NVFP4 and FP8; the BF16 variant resets it to auto.
+    - "--kv-cache-dtype"
+    - "fp8"
+  base_env:
+    # The first NVFP4 start spends about 10 minutes autotuning FlashInfer MoE
+    # kernels, close to the 600 s default engine-ready timeout.
+    VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S: "3600"
+
+features:
+  reasoning:
+    description: "Beam reasoning parser — splits the Harmony `analysis` channel into `reasoning_content`. Reads the checkpoint's `response_template`."
+    args:
+      - "--reasoning-parser"
+      - "beam"
+  tool_calling:
+    description: "Beam tool-call parser with automatic tool choice — tool-call grammar derived from the checkpoint's `response_template`."
+    args:
+      - "--enable-auto-tool-choice"
+      - "--tool-call-parser"
+      - "beam"
+  spec_decoding:
+    label: "DFlash2"
+    description: "DFlash2 speculative decoding with the Beam-trained drafter (DFlash2BeamDraftModel, 5 layers, block size 16), drafting 7 tokens per step. method is dflash; DFlash2 is selected by the draft architecture. The drafter runs on FlashAttention, and adaptive verification checks only the draft tokens likely to be accepted."
+    args:
+      - "--speculative-config"

+      # verification is neutral at low concurrency and helps under load.
+      - '{"method":"dflash","model":"reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","enable_adaptive_verification":true}'

+opt_in_features:
+  - spec_decoding

+variants:
+  # NVFP4 is the default: recommended on Blackwell (TP4) and on H100, where
+  # FP8 fits but leaves little KV-cache headroom. FP8 is recommended on H200.
+  # BF16 needs one 8x B200/B300 node.
+  default:
+    model_id: "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4"
+    precision: nvfp4
+    # Mixed precision (ModelOpt NVFP4 on routed experts only; attention, dense
+    # MLPs, router, embeddings and lm_head stay BF16), so size from the real
+    # checkpoint: 293.6 GB × 1.2 = 352.3 → 353 GB.
+    vram_minimum_gb: 353
+    description: "ModelOpt NVFP4 on the routed experts; all other weights BF16. W4A4 on Blackwell; W4A16 through Marlin on Hopper. Recommended on Blackwell and H100."
+    # NVFP4 defaults to Blackwell-only. On Hopper vLLM runs the FP4 experts
+    # through Marlin (weights dequantized in-kernel, BF16 activations), so
+    # widen the precision constraint to every NVIDIA GPU.

+      brand: NVIDIA

+      - "arch:sm100"
+      - "arch:sm103"
+    # Blackwell runs TP4: 353 GB fits 4x B200 (720 GB) and one GB200/GB300
+    # tray, and TP8 would leave 320 intermediate rows per rank (padded).
+    # Hopper runs TP8.
+    tp:
+      blackwell: 4
+    # Blackwell auto-selects flashinfer_trtllm for the MoE, so only Hopper
+    # needs a pin.
+    hardware_overrides:

+    precision: fp8

+    # checkpoint (503.3 GB) rather than params × 1 byte: × 1.2 = 604.0 → 604 GB.
+    vram_minimum_gb: 604
+    # Per-channel FP8 (compressed-tensors FP8_DYNAMIC, no block structure), so
+    # TP8 has no block_n divisibility constraint.
+    description: "FP8 per-channel weights (compressed-tensors); router, embeddings and lm_head unquantized. Recommended on H200."
+    # Triton MoE measured fastest on B300 and H200; auto would pick CUTLASS
+    # grouped GEMM. Auto-selection already matches the measured attention
+    # (FlashInfer with TRT-LLM kernels on Blackwell, FA3 on Hopper) and FP8
+    # linear (CUTLASS) backends.
+    extra_args:
+      - "--moe-backend"
+      - "triton"
+  bf16:
+    model_id: "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B"
+    precision: bf16

+    # Fits one 8x B300 node (2144 GB); does not fit 8x H200 (1128 GB).
+    vram_minimum_gb: 1204
+    description: "Native BF16 checkpoint (FP32 router weights and expert biases). Requires one 8x B200 or B300 node."
+    # 1204 GB only fits a single 8x B200 (1440 GB) or 8x B300 (2144 GB) node,
+    # and the recipe has no multi-node strategies, so other GPUs can't run it.
+    supported_hardware:
+      - b200
+      - b300

+    # Blackwell auto-selects the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE for BF16 experts.
+    extra_args:
+      - "--kv-cache-dtype"
+      - "auto"
+
+compatible_strategies:

+  - single_node_tep
+  - single_node_dep

+guide: |
+  ## Overview
+
+  [Beam](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B) is Reflection's
+  sparse mixture-of-experts language model, with 501B total parameters and 23B
+  active parameters per token. Its 52 layers combine 512-token sliding-window
+  attention with NoPE full-attention layers, route each token through 8 of 256
+  experts (layers 0-2 use dense MLPs), and support a context length of
+  1,048,576 tokens.
+
+  Beam uses the Harmony message format, with an `analysis` channel for
+  reasoning and a `final` channel for the answer. Generation stops on

+  | Variant | Checkpoint | Weights on disk | Minimum GPU memory | Recommended hardware |
+  |---|---|---|---|---|
+  | NVFP4 (default) | [`reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4`](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4) | 294 GB | 353 GB | 4x B200/B300 or one GB200/GB300 tray (TP4); 8x H100 (TP8, Marlin) |
+  | FP8 | [`reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-FP8`](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-FP8) | 503 GB | 604 GB | 8x H200 (TP8) |
+  | BF16 | [`reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B`](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B) | 1,003 GB | 1,204 GB | 8x B200/B300 (TP8) |
+
+  *Minimum GPU memory* is the weights plus 20% headroom for activations,
+  CUDA graphs and a working KV cache. It is the total across all GPUs, and
+  it is the figure the variant selector above shows.
+
+  The NVFP4 checkpoint quantizes only the routed experts; attention, dense
+  MLPs, the router, embeddings and the LM head stay in BF16. On Blackwell it
+  runs W4A4; on Hopper, vLLM serves the FP4 experts through Marlin with BF16
+  activations.
+
+  ## Prerequisites
+
+  - **vLLM:** the `vllm/vllm-openai:reflection-beam` Docker image. Beam
+    support has not shipped in a vLLM release yet.
+  - **Hardware:** NVIDIA GPUs. Beam's kernels, including a custom all-reduce
+    used with expert parallelism, are CUDA-only.
+  - **Transformers:** the tokenizer uses the Transformers 5 format
+    (`TokenizersBackend`).
+
+  ### Install vLLM
+
+  ```bash
+  docker pull vllm/vllm-openai:reflection-beam
+  ```
+
+  The `vllm serve` commands below run inside this image; the command builder
+  above renders the full `docker run` line.
+
+  ## Launching the server
+
+  ### FP8 with TP8 on H200 or Blackwell
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-FP8 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+    --moe-backend triton \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser beam \
+    --reasoning-parser beam
+  ```
+
+  This is the best-performing FP8 configuration measured on both H200 and
+  B300. Set `--moe-backend triton` explicitly; vLLM otherwise selects CUTLASS
+  for the FP8 MoE. vLLM's default attention backends, FlashAttention 3 on
+  Hopper and FlashInfer with TRT-LLM kernels on Blackwell, are already the
+  fastest measured.
+
+  ### NVFP4 with TP4 on Blackwell
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser beam \
+    --reasoning-parser beam
+  ```
+
+  At TP4 the weights take about 73 GB per GPU, leaving room for the full
+  context window many times over; an 8-GPU node can host two replicas. The
+  first start takes about 10 minutes because FlashInfer autotunes the MoE
+  kernel. That is close to vLLM's default 600 s engine-ready timeout, so the
+  generated command sets `VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600`.
+
+  ### NVFP4 with TP8 on H100
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+    --moe-backend marlin \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser beam \
+    --reasoning-parser beam
+  ```
+
+  Set `--moe-backend marlin` explicitly; it is faster than the backend vLLM
+  selects by default on Hopper. The FP8 checkpoint also fits on 8x H100 but
+  leaves much less memory for the KV cache.
+
+  ### BF16 with TP8 on Blackwell
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B \
+    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser beam \
+    --reasoning-parser beam
+  ```
+
+  ### Tuning
+
+  - **KV cache dtype:** the NVFP4 and FP8 commands use
+    `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, which halves KV memory per token (on 8x H200 with
+    the FP8 checkpoint, about 14M to 28M tokens). The BF16 command keeps the
+    KV cache in BF16.
+  - **Parallelism:** tensor parallelism is the recommended single-node layout.
+    TEP (`--enable-expert-parallel`) and DEP (`--data-parallel-size 8
+    --enable-expert-parallel`) are also supported; DEP is better suited to
+    very large batch sizes.
+
+  ### MegaMoE with attention DP (NVFP4, Blackwell)
+
+  For prefill-heavy, high-concurrency traffic, run attention data-parallel
+  with expert parallelism on FlashInfer's CuTe DSL NVFP4 MegaMoE kernel,
+  which overlaps the expert all-to-all with the expert GEMMs. Start from the
+  NVFP4 command and replace the parallel and MoE settings:
+
+  ```bash
+  vllm serve reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4 \
+    --data-parallel-size 4 \
+    --enable-expert-parallel \
+    --moe-backend flashinfer_moe_ep_cutedsl \
+    --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
+    --enable-auto-tool-choice \
+    --tool-call-parser beam \
+    --reasoning-parser beam
+  ```
+
+  - Only for DEP (`--data-parallel-size` with `--enable-expert-parallel`).
+    It does not support TEP or pure TP.
+  - Use `--data-parallel-size 4` on a GB200/GB300 tray or four B200/B300
+    GPUs, and `8` across a full 8-GPU node.
+  - For low-latency serving, stay on TP4 with `flashinfer_trtllm`.
+
+  ### DFlash2 speculative decoding
+
+  The DFlash2 drafter
+  ([`reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2`](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2))
+  shares the target model's embeddings and LM head:
+
+  ```bash
+  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"FLASH_ATTN","enable_adaptive_verification":true}'
+  ```
+
+  With `enable_adaptive_verification`, vLLM predicts how likely each draft
+  token is to be accepted and verifies only the ones worth the compute,
+  rather than all 7 every step. It makes little difference at low
+  concurrency and raises throughput under load. Remove it to verify the
+  full draft every step.
+
+  The drafter supports up to 15 speculative tokens; 7 is recommended. It
+  speeds up decoding most at low concurrency and adds about 1.7 GB per GPU,
+  which reduces KV-cache capacity. Acceptance depends on natural-language
+  input, so benchmark it with a real-text dataset rather than
+  `--dataset-name random`.
+
+  ### Output constraints
+
+  By default, the `beam` output grammar constrains every assistant turn from
+  its first token (reasoning, then an answer or a tool call). Set
+  `VLLM_BEAM_ALWAYS_CONSTRAIN_OUTPUT=0` to disable it.
+
+  ## Client usage
+
+  ```bash
+  curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -d '{
+      "model": "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4",
+      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello."}]
+    }'
+  ```
+
+  Set `model` to the checkpoint being served: `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4`,
+  `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-FP8`, or `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B` for
+  BF16. `/v1/models` lists the served name.
+
+  ### Reasoning effort
+
+  Beam reasons at the maximum effort, `max` (512), unless the request sets
+  `reasoning_effort`:
+
+  ```bash
+  curl http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions \
+    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
+    -d '{
+      "model": "reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4",
+      "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "What is 17 * 19?"}],
+      "reasoning_effort": "low"
+    }'
+  ```
+
+  The Rust frontend (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`) serves `/v1/chat/completions`
+  and `/v1/completions`, but not yet `/v1/responses` or the Anthropic-compatible
+  `/v1/messages` (both return 404). Use the default Python frontend for those
+  APIs.
+
+  ## References
+
+  - [Beam model card](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B)
+  - [Beam FP8](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-FP8)
+  - [Beam NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4)
+  - [DFlash2 drafter](https://huggingface.co/reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2)
